newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY LOOK TO CONTINUE GOLD RUSH.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY LOOK TO CONTINUE GOLD RUSH.

text.p: Deborah Compagnoni did her part, now it will be up to Isolde Kostner to carry Italy's dominance of the women's competition into the second week of the Alpine world championships.

Compagnoni kicked off the opening week with wins in the slalom and giant slalom and if Kostner can pick up where her team mate left off, with a victory in Tuesday's super-G, it would leave the Italians in position to become the first nation since Switzerland in 1985 to sweep the women's gold medals.
Although Kostner enters the race holding down third place in the super-G standings behind Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg and Germany's Hilde Gerg, many rate her the favourite on recent performance.
After getting the season off to a slow start with a 13th place in Lake Louise, Canada, Kostner has made steady progress recording fifth, third, second and first place finishes, in that order.

"I want to race as soon as possible in one of my disciplines," said Kostner, after a seventh place finish in Sunday's giant slalom. "I had a look at the super-G course today and it made me want to race even more. I'm feeling really good and I'm ready to go."
While Kostner will be looking to keep Italy on a roll, Wiberg will be hoping she can get back on track.

Wiberg, the runaway leader in the women's overall World Cup, was expected to be a dominant figure here, but has yet to find her form, crashing out in the slalom and crossing a disappointing sixth in the giant slalom.

The 26-year-old Swede, however, has maintained that her focus at these championships has always been the second week which includes the super-G and downhill, the only two events in which she has not won world championship or Olympic gold.
The super-G in fact may well represent Wiberg's best chance at a sixth gold medal having won two-of-five World Cup races this season and placed second in two others.
"I'm looking forward to the super-G because I think it's a course that suits me," said Wiberg. "In fact I'm looking forward to this whole week with the downhill and the combined.
"I was too tense at the start of the championships and now I've had time to relax."
Gerg, a model of consistency has not finished outside the top five in all five events this season but it is her team mate Katja Seizinger, the Olympic downhill champion, who many fear most.
Seizinger, the 1993 super-G world champion and Olympic bronze medallist, has not won a race this season but still ranks herself among the favourites this year.

"The super-G and giant slalom are two different things," said Seizinger, who suffered a mild concussion after a high speed spill in the final downhill before the start of the championships. "This is a new race and there are new favourites.
"The top five from the World Cup are favourites and I'm among them.
"But in the super-G I've lost a little ground, I'm not the top favourite like I was last year."
